claim: Two parallel pathways produce cholesterol: the Bloch and Kandutsch-Russell pathways.
source: Two parallel pathways produce cholesterol: the Bloch and Kandutsch-Russell pathways.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about cholesterol biosynthesis pathways.

claim: No tissue used the canonical K–R pathway.
source: Surprisingly, no tissue used the canonical K–R pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study using stable isotope labeling and isotopomer analysis in mice.

claim: A hybrid pathway called the modified K–R (MK–R) pathway was identified.
source: Rather, a hybrid pathway was identified that we call the modified K–R (MK–R) pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data showing a different pathway architecture than previously described.

claim: Proportional flux through the Bloch pathway varied from 8% in preputial gland to 97% in testes.
source: Proportional flux through the Bloch pathway varied from 8% in preputial gland to 97% in testes
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the in vivo flux analysis in different mouse tissues.

claim: The tissue-specificity observed in vivo was retained in cultured cells.
source: the tissue-specificity observed in vivo was retained in cultured cells.
evidence: This is based on experimental comparison of pathway utilization in tissues versus cultured cells from those tissues.

claim: The distribution of sterol isotopomers in plasma mirrored that of liver.
source: The distribution of sterol isotopomers in plasma mirrored that of liver.
evidence: This is a finding from simultaneous measurement of sterol turnover in plasma and liver of mice.

claim: Sterol depletion in cultured cells increased flux through the Bloch pathway.
source: Sterol depletion in cultured cells increased flux through the Bloch pathway
evidence: This is based on experimental data comparing sterol flux in cells grown in cholesterol-depleted versus cholesterol-replete medium.

claim: Overexpression of 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR24) enhanced usage of the MK–R pathway.
source: overexpression of 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR24) enhanced usage of the MK–R pathway.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from transfection experiments showing altered pathway utilization.

claim: Relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is highly variable.
source: Thus, relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is highly variable
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the range of pathway utilization observed across different tissues and conditions.

claim: Relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is tissue-specific.
source: Thus, relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is highly variable, tissue-specific
evidence: This is based on the observation of different pathway utilization patterns across different tissues.

claim: Relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is flux dependent.
source: Thus, relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is highly variable, tissue-specific, flux dependent
evidence: This is based on observations that pathway utilization changes with changes in cholesterol synthesis rates.

claim: Relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is epigenetically fixed.
source: Thus, relative use of the Bloch and MK–R pathways is highly variable, tissue-specific, flux dependent, and epigenetically fixed.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cultured cells retain the pathway preferences of their tissue of origin.

claim: Maintenance of two interdigitated pathways permits production of diverse bioactive sterols that can be regulated independently of cholesterol.
source: Maintenance of two interdigitated pathways permits production of diverse bioactive sterols that can be regulated independently of cholesterol.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of having two pathways.

claim: Cholesterol is an essential structural component of vertebrate cell membranes.
source: Cholesterol is an essential structural component of vertebrate cell membranes (Maxfield and Tabas, 2005)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Cholesterol is a precursor of bile acids.
source: a precursor of vital end products such as bile acids (Russell, 2009)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Cholesterol is a precursor of steroid hormones.
source: a precursor of vital end products such as bile acids (Russell, 2009) and steroid hormones (Sih and Whitlock, 1968).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Cholesterol was first identified as a crystalline component of gallstones more than 200 years ago.
source: First identified as a crystalline component of gallstones more than 200 years ago
evidence: This is historical knowledge about cholesterol discovery.

claim: Cholesterol consists of a rigid, planar tetracyclic nucleus and a flexible, iso-octyl side-chain at carbon 17.
source: cholesterol consists of a rigid, planar tetracyclic nucleus and a flexible, iso-octyl side-chain at carbon 17 (Nes, 2011).
evidence: This is structural information about cholesterol supported by a citation.

claim: Cholesterol is synthesized entirely from acetate through a complex series of over 30 enzymatic reactions.
source: The molecule is synthesized entirely from acetate through a complex series of over 30 enzymatic reactions
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about cholesterol biosynthesis.

claim: Cholesterol biosynthesis involves four major processes: condensation of acetate to isoprene, polymerization of isoprene to squalene, cyclization of squalene to lanosterol, and conversion of lanosterol to cholesterol.
source: that are clustered into four major processes: condensation of acetate to isoprene, polymerization of isoprene to squalene, cyclization of squalene to lanosterol, and finally the conversion of lanosterol to cholesterol
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about the stages of cholesterol biosynthesis.

claim: Bloch et al. (1965) proposed that reduction of the double bond in the side chain (Δ24) is the last reaction in the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway.
source: Bloch et al. (1965) proposed that reduction of the double bond in the side chain (Δ24) is the last reaction in the pathway
evidence: This is a historical claim about the Bloch pathway supported by citation.

claim: In the Bloch pathway, cholesterol synthesis proceeds via a series of side-chain unsaturated intermediates to desmosterol, which is reduced by DHCR24 to cholesterol.
source: Thus, in the Bloch pathway, cholesterol synthesis proceeds via a series of side-chain unsaturated intermediates to desmosterol, which is reduced by DHCR24 to cholesterol.
evidence: This describes the established Bloch pathway mechanism.

claim: Kandutsch and Russell reported that the preputial glands of mice synthesized dihydrolanosterol and other side-chain saturated intermediates different from those in the Bloch pathway.
source: Subsequently, Kandutsch and Russell (Kandutsch and Russell, 1960a, 1960b) reported that the preputial glands of mice synthesized dihydrolanosterol and other side-chain saturated intermediates that were different from those in the Bloch pathway.
evidence: This is a historical finding supported by citations.

claim: In the Kandutsch–Russell (K–R) pathway, the Δ24 bond of lanosterol is reduced and the conversion of dihydrolanosterol to cholesterol proceeds via 7-dehydrocholesterol using the same enzymes as the Bloch pathway.
source: They proposed an alternative pathway, the Kandutsch–Russell (K–R) pathway, in which the Δ24 bond of lanosterol is reduced and the conversion of dihydrolanosterol to cholesterol proceeds via 7-dehydrocholesterol (Figure 1, red arrows) using the same enzymes as the Bloch pathway.
evidence: This describes the K-R pathway as originally proposed, supported by citations.

claim: Later studies showed the presence of saturated side chain intermediates in brain, skin, and eventually in all tissues examined.
source: Later studies showed the presence of saturated side chain intermediates in brain, skin, and eventually in all tissues examined (Schroepfer, 1982).
evidence: This is a historical finding supported by citation.

claim: Much less is known about the relative use and physiological significance of the Bloch and K–R pathways compared to the catalytic mechanisms and regulation of the enzymes.
source: The catalytic mechanisms and regulation of the enzymes that catalyze the Bloch and K–R pathways have been extensively investigated but much less is known about their relative use and physiological significance.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Cholesterol biosynthesis is usually measured using radioisotope methods that are highly sensitive but do not provide information about the turnover of intermediate sterols in the biosynthetic pathway.
source: Cholesterol biosynthesis is usually measured using radioisotope methods (Dietschy and Spady, 1984) that are highly sensitive but do not provide information about the turnover of intermediate sterols in the biosynthetic pathway.
evidence: This describes the limitations of traditional methods, supported by citation.

claim: Flux through the Bloch and K–R pathways has not been systematically studied in cultured cells or in vivo.
source: Flux through the Bloch and K–R pathways has not been systematically studied in cultured cells or in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that this study addresses.

claim: The relative use of the two pathways and their responses to changes in cholesterol availability are not known.
source: Therefore, the relative use of the two pathways and their responses to changes in cholesterol availability are not known.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge.

claim: The reason why both pathways have been maintained is not known.
source: The reason why both pathways have been maintained is also not known.
evidence: This is a statement about an unanswered question in the field.

claim: The biosynthetic intermediates of the two pathways have powerful, but distinct, effects on cholesterol homeostasis.
source: The biosynthetic intermediates of the two pathways have powerful, but distinct, effects on cholesterol homeostasis (Yang et al., 2006; Lange et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The biosynthetic intermediates of the two pathways have effects on fatty acid synthesis.
source: The biosynthetic intermediates of the two pathways have powerful, but distinct, effects on cholesterol homeostasis (Yang et al., 2006; Lange et al., 2008), fatty acid synthesis (Spann et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The biosynthetic intermediates of the two pathways have effects on inflammation.
source: The biosynthetic intermediates of the two pathways have powerful, but distinct, effects on cholesterol homeostasis (Yang et al., 2006; Lange et al., 2008), fatty acid synthesis (Spann et al., 2012), and inflammation (Spann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Varying the concentrations of specific cholesterol biosynthetic intermediates by differential use of the Bloch and K–R pathways may contribute to regulation of diverse cellular processes.
source: Varying the concentrations of specific cholesterol biosynthetic intermediates by differential use of the Bloch and K–R pathways may thus contribute to regulation of diverse cellular processes.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the functional significance of pathway variation.

claim: Kelleher and Masterson (1992) demonstrated that stable isotope methods and isotopomer spectral analysis (ISA) could be used to measure the flux of cholesterol biosynthetic intermediates such as lathosterol in cultured cells and in living animals using gas chromatography–MS.
source: Kelleher and Masterson (1992) demonstrated that stable isotope methods and isotopomer spectral analysis (ISA) could be used to measure the flux of cholesterol biosynthetic intermediates such as lathosterol in cultured cells and in living animals using gas chromatography–MS (Lindenthal et al., 2002).
evidence: This describes a methodological advance supported by citations.

claim: McDonald et al. (2012) developed a liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method to determine steady-state concentrations of most of post squalene cholesterol biosynthetic intermediates of the Bloch and K–R pathways in biological fluids.
source: More recently, McDonald et al. (2012) developed a liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) method to determine steady-state concentrations of most of post squalene cholesterol biosynthetic intermediates of the Bloch and K–R pathways in biological fluids.
evidence: This describes a methodological advance supported by citation.

claim: In unlabeled SV-589 cells, the isotopomer spectrum of lanosterol matched the predicted distribution based on a 1.1% natural abundance of 13C and a 0.015% natural abundance of deuterium.
source: In unlabeled cells, the isotopomer spectrum matched the predicted distribution based on a 1.1% natural abundance of 13C and a 0.015% natural abundance of deuterium (Figure 2A, top, left panel).

claim: Lanosterol molecules containing exclusively 12C, 16O and 1H isotopes had an m/z peak of 409 Da (M = 0) and comprised 72% of the total in unlabeled cells.
source: Lanosterol molecules containing exclusively 12C, 16O and 1H isotopes had an m/z peak of 409 Da (M = 0) and comprised 72% of the total.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: After cells were grown in 5% D2O for 24 hr, only 25% of the lanosterol had not incorporated any deuterium atoms (M = 0).
source: After cells were grown in 5% D2O long enough for the lanosterol pool to be replaced (in this case, for 24 hr), only 25% of the lanosterol had not incorporated any deuterium atoms (M = 0).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the D2O labeling experiment.

claim: The addition of 25-OH Chol to the medium decreased the rate of lanosterol biosynthesis by 90%.
source: The addition of 25-OH Chol to the medium decreased the rate of lanosterol biosynthesis by 90% (Figure 2A, bottom).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the experiment testing the effect of 25-hydroxycholesterol.

claim: Deuterium was incorporated almost exclusively into Bloch pathway intermediates in Y1BS1 cells.
source: Deuterium was incorporated almost exclusively into Bloch pathway intermediates in Y1BS1 cells
evidence: This is a finding from the D2O labeling experiment in Y1BS1 cells.

claim: The rates of incorporation were similar for lanosterol, ff-MAS, t-MAS, dehydrodesmosterol, and desmosterol in Y1BS1 cells.
source: in which the rates of incorporation were similar for lanosterol, ff-MAS, t-MAS, dehydrodesmosterol, and desmosterol (Figure 2B, top left panel).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the flux analysis in Y1BS1 cells.

claim: Little turnover of K–R intermediates was detected in Y1BS1 cells.
source: Little turnover of K–R intermediates was detected in these cells (Figure 2B, top right panel).
evidence: This is a finding from the flux analysis in Y1BS1 cells.

source: In SV-589 fibroblasts (Figure 2B, bottom panel), lanosterol was quantitatively converted to ff-MAS and t-MAS (Bloch pathway) with almost no detectable incorporation into the corresponding K–R intermediates (dihydro-ff-MAS and dihydro-t-MAS).
evidence: This is a finding from the flux analysis in SV-589 cells.

claim: Incorporation into the downstream Bloch intermediates dehydrodesmosterol and desmosterol was minimal in SV-589 fibroblasts, but robust labeling of 7-dehydrocholesterol was observed.
source: Incorporation into the downstream Bloch intermediates dehydrodesmosterol and desmosterol was minimal, but robust labeling of 7-dehydrocholesterol was observed
evidence: This is a finding from the flux analysis in SV-589 cells.

claim: In SV-589 fibroblasts, there is a crossover from the Bloch to the K–R pathway between t-MAS and dehydrodesmosterol.
source: indicating a crossover from the Bloch to the K–R pathway between t-MAS and dehydrodesmosterol (Figure 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of deuterium incorporation into different intermediates.

claim: The methylated biosynthetic intermediates between lanosterol and 7-dehydrocholesterol in the K–R pathway (i.e., dihydrolanosterol, dihydro-ff-MAS, and dihydro-t-MAS) did not turnover at comparable rates to either lanosterol or 7-dehydrocholesterol in SV-589 cells.
source: The methylated biosynthetic intermediates between lanosterol and 7-dehydrocholesterol in the K–R pathway (i.e., dihydrolanosterol, dihydro-ff-MAS, and dihydro-t-MAS) did not turnover at comparable rates to either lanosterol or 7-dehydrocholesterol
evidence: This is a finding from the flux analysis in SV-589 cells.

claim: The classical K–R pathway was not used to synthesize cholesterol in SV-589 cells.
source: suggesting that the classical K–R pathway was not used to synthesize cholesterol in these cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of sterol turnover observed.

claim: In SV-589 cells, intermediates proceed down the Bloch pathway until demethylation of the sterol nucleus is complete, and then they undergo reduction of the double bond at C24 to enter the K–R pathway.
source: Instead, the cells used a hybrid pathway that we will refer to as the modified Kandutsch–Russell (MK–R) pathway. In this hybrid pathway, intermediates proceed down the Bloch pathway until demethylation of the sterol nucleus is complete, and then they undergo reduction of the double bond at C24 to enter the K–R pathway.

claim: In SV-589 cells, the cross-over to the MK–R pathway occurs at either zymosterol, dehydrolathosterol, or dehydrodesmosterol.
source: Therefore, in cultured fibroblasts the cross-over to the MK–R pathway occurs at either zymosterol, dehydrolathosterol, or dehydrodesmosterol.
evidence: This is inferred from the data, though the exact intermediate could not be pinpointed.

claim: In WT CHO-7 cells, the Bloch pathway accounted for ∼90% of cholesterol synthesis.
source: In WT CHO-7 cells, the Bloch pathway accounted for ∼90% of cholesterol synthesis (Figure 3A).

claim: Deletion of SCAP reduced lanosterol biosynthesis by 80% in SRD13A cells.
source: Deletion of SCAP reduced lanosterol biosynthesis by 80%, with similar reductions in the biosynthesis of other unsaturated side chain Bloch intermediates (Figure 3A).

claim: Despite the massive reduction in net sterol synthesis in the SRD13A cells, the biosynthetic rate of 7-dehydrocholesterol was similar to that observed in the parental cell line.
source: Despite the massive reduction in net sterol synthesis in the SRD13A cells, the biosynthetic rate of 7-dehydrocholesterol was similar to that observed in the parental cell line (Figure 3A, inset).

claim: Flux through the MK–R pathway is constitutive in SRD13A cells.
source: This finding suggests the flux through the MK–R pathway is constitutive in these cells.

source: In cultured human hepatoma cells (HuH-7 cells) grown in cholesterol-replete serum (FCS) (Figure 3B), the pattern of sterol turnover resembled that seen in SV-589 cells (Figure 2B); most of the sterol flux traversed the MK–R biosynthetic pathway (Figure 3B, open bars).

claim: When HuH7 cells were grown in cholesterol-depleted serum (NCLPPS), sterol turnover doubled.
source: When cells were grown for 16 hr in cholesterol-depleted serum (NCLPPS) to stimulate cholesterol biosynthesis, sterol turnover doubled.

source: Essentially all of the increase occurred via the Bloch pathway: flux through the MK–R pathway did not change (Figure 3B, open bars).

claim: Cholesterol depletion shifted the relative utilization of the two pathways in HuH7 cells such that approximately equal amounts of lanosterol were metabolized via Bloch and MK–R intermediates.
source: Therefore, cholesterol depletion shifted the relative utilization of the two pathways such that approximately equal amounts of lanosterol were metabolized via Bloch and MK–R intermediates.

claim: Cholesterol depletion resulted in the incorporation of a small amount of deuterium into dihydrolanosterol in HuH7 cells.
source: Cholesterol depletion also resulted in the incorporation of a small amount of deuterium into dihydrolanosterol, presumably reflecting conversion from lanosterol

claim: None of the other K–R intermediates prior to 7-dehydrocholesterol were labeled in HuH7 cells.
source: but none of the other K–R intermediates prior to 7-dehydrocholesterol were labeled in these cells.

claim: The increase in flux through the Bloch pathway cannot be attributed simply to changes in the expression of SREBP-2 and the coordinated transcriptional upregulation of genes encoding enzymes in the pathway.
source: Thus, the increase in flux through the Bloch pathway cannot be attributed simply to changes in the expression of SREBP-2 and the coordinated transcriptional upregulation of genes encoding enzymes in the pathway.

claim: In HEK-293 cells transfected with vector alone, 78% of cholesterol biosynthesis proceeded through the Bloch pathway.
source: In HEK-293 cells transfected with vector alone, 78% of cholesterol biosynthesis proceeded through the Bloch pathway (Figure 4A, open bars).

source: Overexpression of DHCR24 resulted in lanosterol being quantitatively converted into the Bloch pathway intermediate zymosterol

source: but did not increase incorporation of label into the early methyl sterols of the classic K–R pathway.

claim: No evidence was seen of utilization of the classical K–R pathway in HEK-293 cells overexpressing DHCR24.
source: No evidence was seen of utilization of the classical K–R pathway under these conditions.

source: In cells expressing vector alone, the d6 label appeared in unsaturated side chain sterols of the Bloch pathway, with little to no label appearing in the MK–R intermediates (Figure 4B, open bars in upper panel).

source: In cells expressing DHCR24, the d6 label was detected in lanosterol, ff-MAS, t-MAS, and zymosterol, but not in the downstream Bloch intermediates (Figure 4B, closed bars in upper panel).

claim: The MK–R pathway predominated in skin.
source: In contrast to adrenal glands, the MK–R pathway predominated in skin.

claim: The synthesis of desmosterol was much less than either lanosterol or 7-dehydrocholesterol in skin.
source: The synthesis of desmosterol was much less than either lanosterol or 7-dehydrocholesterol (Figure 5).

claim: There was measureable synthesis of dihydro-t-MAS in skin, indicating that saturation of the side chain double bond can occur before total demethylation of t-MAS.

evidence: This is a finding from the in vivo flux analysis in skin, with inference about the pathway.

claim: In liver, the rates of synthesis of desmosterol and 7-dehydrocholesterol were similar.
source: In liver, the rates of synthesis of desmosterol and 7-dehydrocholesterol were similar.

source: Thus, approximately half of the sterol flux followed the Bloch pathway, whereas the other half used the MK–R pathway.

claim: Dihydrolanosterol was synthesized in liver at ∼5–10% the rate of lanosterol synthesis (2 ng/μg tissue/day).
source: In contrast to all other tissues examined, dihydrolanosterol was synthesized in liver at ∼5–10% the rate of lanosterol synthesis (2 ng/μg tissue/day).

claim: Essentially no synthesis of dihydro-ff-MAS was detected in liver.
source: Essentially no synthesis of dihydro-ff-MAS was detected.
evidence: This is a finding from the in vivo flux analysis in liver.

claim: A fraction of hepatic lanosterol was converted to dihydrolanosterol but did not proceed down the K–R pathway.
source: This result suggests that a fraction of hepatic lanosterol was converted to dihydrolanosterol but did not proceed down the K–R pathway.

claim: Cultured human hepatocytes (HuH7 cells) also synthesized dihydolanosterol that was not further metabolized into dihydro-ff-MAS.
source: Consistent with this finding, cultured human hepatocytes (HuH7 cells) also synthesized dihydolanosterol that was not further metabolized into dihydro-ff-MAS (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell culture experiments that is consistent with the in vivo liver data.

claim: ∼5–10% of the sterol synthesized in liver or in cultured hepatocytes is converted to dihydrolanosterol and exits the cholesterol biosynthetic pathway.
source: Thus ∼5–10% of the sterol synthesized in liver or in cultured hepatocytes is converted to dihydrolanosterol and exits the cholesterol biosynthetic pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the flux data in liver and hepatocytes.

claim: The K–R pathway was first described in preputial gland.
source: The K–R pathway was first described in preputial gland, a modified sebaceous gland that is present in rodents but not in humans (Kandutsch and Russell, 1960a, 1960b).

claim: The turnover of 7-dehydrocholesterol in preputial glands was similar to that of lanosterol.
source: We found that the turnover of 7-dehydrocholesterol in preputial glands was similar to that of lanosterol
evidence: This is a finding from the in vivo flux analysis in preputial glands.

claim: The finding that turnover of 7-dehydrocholesterol in preputial glands was similar to that of lanosterol is consistent with the findings of Kandutsch and Russell.
source: which is consistent with the findings of Kandutsch and Russell (2).
evidence: This compares the current findings to historical work.

claim: The data from preputial glands are not consistent with the K–R pathway as it was originally described.
source: Nevertheless, our data are not consistent with the K–R pathway as it was originally described.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the flux data in preputial glands.

claim: The flux from lanosterol in preputial glands proceeded via the Bloch pathway intermediates ff-MAS and t-MAS without any detectable incorporation into the corresponding saturated side chain sterols (dihydrolanosterol and dihydro-ff-MAS).
source: The flux from lanosterol proceeded via the Bloch pathway intermediates ff-MAS and t-MAS without any detectable incorporation into the corresponding saturated side chain sterols (dihydrolanosterol and dihydro-ff-MAS).
evidence: This is a finding from the in vivo flux analysis in preputial glands.

claim: Even in preputial glands, lanosterol demethylation commences before side-chain saturation.
source: Therefore, even in preputial glands, lanosterol demethylation commences before side-chain saturation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pattern of sterol flux in preputial glands.

claim: A similar pattern of sterol flux through the MK–R pathway was measured in the skin and brain.
source: A similar pattern of sterol flux through the MK–R pathway was measured in the skin and brain.
evidence: This is a comparative finding from the in vivo flux analysis.

claim: In the brain, the absolute rate of cholesterol synthesis was low, corresponding to less than 2% of that observed in liver.
source: In the brain, the absolute rate of cholesterol synthesis was low, corresponding to less than 2% of that observed in liver (Figure 5, bottom panel; note differences in scale).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the in vivo flux analysis comparing brain and liver.

claim: Like the skin and preputial gland, the MK–R pathway for cholesterol synthesis predominated in the central nervous system.
source: Like the skin and preputial gland, the MK–R pathway for cholesterol synthesis predominated in the central nervous system
evidence: This is a finding from the in vivo flux analysis in brain.

claim: The brain was reported previously to express very low levels of DHCR24.
source: even though the brain was reported previously to express very low levels of DHCR24 (Nes, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: None of the tissues examined in this study utilized the classic K–R pathway.
source: Thus, none of the tissues examined in this study utilized the classic K–R pathway.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the in vivo flux analysis across all tissues.

claim: Sterols were demethylated, at least partially, before the side chain was saturated in all tissues examined.
source: Instead, sterols were demethylated, at least partially, before the side chain was saturated.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the in vivo flux analysis across all tissues.

claim: The fractional utilization of the Bloch pathway ranged from 0.97 (testes) to 0.08 (preputial gland).
source: The values obtained ranged from 0.97 (testes) to 0.08 (preputial gland) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of pathway utilization across tissues.

claim: In general, tissues with a higher lanosterol synthesis rate had a higher fractional utilization of the Bloch pathway.
source: In general, tissues with a higher lanosterol synthesis rate had a higher fractional utilization of the Bloch pathway (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is a correlation observed in the data across tissues.

claim: Skin and preputial gland are exceptions to the general pattern, having high sterol synthesis rates via the MK–R pathway.
source: with the exception of the skin and preputial gland, which had high sterol synthesis rates via the MK–R pathway.
evidence: This is an observation of exceptions to the general correlation.

claim: It has been suggested that relative usage of the Bloch and K–R pathway is determined by level of expression of DHCR24.
source: It has been suggested that relative usage of the Bloch and K–R pathway is determined by level of expression of DHCR24 (Nes, 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The tissue with the highest level of both DHCR24 mRNA and protein was the preputial gland.
source: The tissue with the highest level of both DHCR24 mRNA and protein was the preputial gland, which also has highest fractional utilization of the MK–R pathway (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene and protein expression analysis.

claim: The tissue with the second highest level of DHCR24 mRNA and protein was the liver.
source: Surprisingly, the tissue with the second highest level of DHCR24 mRNA and protein was the liver, which predominantly utilizes the Bloch pathway (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene and protein expression analysis that is surprising given the pathway utilization.

claim: Skin had mRNA and protein levels of DHCR24 that were lower than those found in the liver.
source: Skin, which has the second highest fractional usage of the MK–R pathway for cholesterol biosynthesis, had mRNA and protein levels of DHCR24 that were lower than those found in the liver.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene and protein expression analysis.

claim: In the brain the level of DHCR24 mRNA was higher than that detected in the skin and yet no protein was detected in this tissue.
source: In the brain the level of DHCR24 mRNA was higher than that detected in the skin and yet no protein was detected in this tissue.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene and protein expression analysis showing discordance between mRNA and protein.

claim: The level of DHCR24 mRNA in tissues did not always correlate with the fractional utilization of the MK–R pathway.
source: Thus, the level of DHCR24 mRNA in tissues did not always correlate with the fractional utilization of the MK–R pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing DHCR24 expression with pathway utilization across tissues.

claim: DHCR24 was expressed at very low levels in tissues that predominantly use the Bloch pathway (testes, spleen, adrenal and adipose tissue).
source: In general, DHCR24 was expressed at very low levels in tissues that predominantly use the Bloch pathway (testes, spleen, adrenal and adipose tissue)
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: DHCR24 was expressed at very low levels in tissues with low cholesterol biosynthetic rates (heart and muscle).
source: and in those with low cholesterol biosynthetic rates (heart and muscle) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: In mammals, liver is the major source of plasma cholesterol.
source: In mammals, liver is the major source of plasma cholesterol (Dietschy and Turley, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The fractions of sterols with incorporated label in plasma and liver were remarkably similar for lanosterol, desmosterol, and 7-dehydrocholesterol.
source: We found that the fractions of sterols with incorporated label in plasma and liver were remarkably similar for lanosterol, desmosterol, and 7-dehydrocholesterol (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the simultaneous measurement of sterol turnover in plasma and liver.

claim: The only sterol for which the labeling pattern was substantially different between plasma and liver was dihydrolanosterol.
source: The only sterol for which the labeling pattern was substantially different between the two compartments was dihydrolanosterol, which readily incorporated label in liver but remained unlabeled in plasma.
evidence: This is a finding from the simultaneous measurement of sterol turnover in plasma and liver.

claim: The testes and adrenal gland utilize the canonical Bloch pathway almost exclusively.
source: The testes and adrenal gland utilize the canonical Bloch pathway (Bloch, 1965) almost exclusively (Figure 8, black arrows).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the in vivo flux analysis.

claim: A hybrid pathway named the MK–R pathway exists in skin, preputial glands and brain.
source: A hybrid pathway that we have named the MK–R pathway exists in skin, preputial glands and brain, (Figure 8, red arrows).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the in vivo flux analysis.

claim: In skin, preputial glands and brain, sterols undergo demethylation prior to side chain saturation.
source: In these tissues, sterols undergo demethylation prior to side chain saturation (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the in vivo flux analysis.

claim: Experiments using deuterium-labeled lanosterol and zymosterol in HEK-293 cells confirmed that zymosterol is the first sterol to undergo appreciable side-chain reduction, at least in these cells.
source: Whereas we were not able to localize the specific DHCR24 substrate in the D2O labeling studies, experiments using deuterium-labeled lanosterol and zymosterol in HEK-293 cells confirmed that zymosterol is the first sterol to undergo appreciable side-chain reduction, at least in these cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the labeled sterol experiments.

claim: Immortalized cells in culture retained the specific pathways used by their tissues of origin.
source: Remarkably, immortalized cells in culture retained the specific pathways used by their tissues of origin.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing pathway utilization in tissues versus cultured cells.

claim: Regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis was achieved almost exclusively by changes in flux through the Bloch pathway.
source: Regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis was achieved almost exclusively by changes in flux through the Bloch pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experiments examining effects of cholesterol depletion and SCAP deletion.

claim: The MK–R pathway is consistent with a reaction sequence proposed by Bae and Paik (1997).
source: The MK–R pathway is consistent with a reaction sequence proposed by Bae and Paik (1997), who reported that zymosterol was preferred over lanosterol as a substrate for C-24-reduction in rat liver microsomes.
evidence: This compares the current findings to a prior hypothesis, supported by citation.

claim: Bae and Paik hypothesized that the physiological pathway for conversion of lanosterol to cholesterol did not correspond to either the Bloch or the KR pathways, but rather to a reaction sequence in which C24-reduction occurred after demethylation but before the final Δ5-dehydrogenation and Δ7-reduction of the sterol nucleus.
source: Those authors hypothesized that the physiological pathway for conversion of lanosterol to cholesterol did not correspond to either the Bloch or the KR pathways, but rather to a reaction sequence in which C24-reduction occurred after demethylation but before the final Δ5-dehydrogenation and Δ7-reduction of the sterol nucleus.
evidence: This describes a prior hypothesis from the literature.

claim: The proposal by Bae and Paik was not assessed in vivo and did not gain wide acceptance.
source: This proposal was not assessed in vivo and did not gain wide acceptance.
evidence: This is a statement about the reception of prior work.

claim: The present data provide in vivo evidence for 24-reduction of zymosterol.
source: The present data provide in vivo evidence for 24-reduction of zymosterol
evidence: This is a conclusion from the in vivo flux analysis.

claim: The predominance of the Bloch pathway in most tissues with high rates of cholesterol synthesis indicates that desmosterol is a major physiological substrate for DHCR24.
source: but the predominance of the Bloch pathway in most tissues with high rates of cholesterol synthesis indicates that desmosterol is a major physiological substrate for the enzyme.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that tissues with high cholesterol synthesis predominantly use the Bloch pathway.

claim: Reduced cellular cholesterol content selectively upregulated the Bloch pathway in cultured CHO7 and HuH7 cells.
source: Reduced cellular cholesterol content selectively upregulated the Bloch pathway in cultured CHO7 and HuH7 cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell culture experiments.

claim: Genetic ablation of SCAP dramatically reduced flux through the Bloch pathway, but had virtually no effect on the MK–R pathway.
source: Genetic ablation of SCAP, which is required for SREBP activation (Rawson et al., 1999), dramatically reduced flux through the Bloch pathway, but had virtually no effect on the MK–R pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from the SCAP-deficient cell experiments.

claim: Depletion of cellular cholesterol by incubation in NCLPPS resulted in a major increase in flux through the Bloch pathway with no detectable change in flux through the MK–R pathway.
source: Similarly, depletion of cellular cholesterol by incubation in NCLPPS resulted in a major increase in flux through the Bloch pathway with no detectable change in flux through the MK–R pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from the cholesterol depletion experiments.

claim: The MK–R pathway is constitutively active.
source: These findings suggest that the MK–R pathway is constitutively active
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that MK-R flux does not change with cholesterol depletion or SCAP deletion.

claim: The Bloch pathway is used preferentially for regulated cholesterol biosynthesis in response to fluctuations in cholesterol availability and demand.
source: and that the Bloch pathway is used preferentially for regulated cholesterol biosynthesis in response to fluctuations in cholesterol availability and demand.
evidence: This is inferred from the selective upregulation of the Bloch pathway with cholesterol depletion.

claim: Upregulation of the Bloch pathway increases the synthesis of regulatory sterols that limit cholesterol accumulation in the cells.
source: Upregulation of the Bloch pathway also increases the synthesis of regulatory sterols that limit cholesterol accumulation in the cells
evidence: This is a functional interpretation of the pathway regulation.

claim: Desmosterol activates LXR, which promotes cholesterol efflux from cells.
source: desmosterol activates LXR, which promotes cholesterol efflux from cells, and acts as a feedback inhibitor of cholesterol synthesis by inactivating SREBP (Yang et al., 2006; Spann et al., 2012).

claim: Desmosterol acts as a feedback inhibitor of cholesterol synthesis by inactivating SREBP.
source: desmosterol activates LXR, which promotes cholesterol efflux from cells, and acts as a feedback inhibitor of cholesterol synthesis by inactivating SREBP (Yang et al., 2006; Spann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

source: In the adrenal glands, lanosterol was quantitatively converted to desmosterol, and then presumably to cholesterol, which provides the substrate for adrenal steroidogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the flux analysis in adrenal glands with inference about the function.

source: In contrast, only one-third of the lanosterol synthesized in the testes was converted to desmosterol, and virtually none entered the MK–R pathway.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the flux analysis in testes.

source: In this tissue, lanosterol was quantitatively converted to ff-MAS and then to t-MAS, but more than two-thirds of the t-MAS was diverted from the pathway before zymosterol (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the flux analysis in testes.

claim: t-MAS and its immediate precursor ff-MAS have been implicated as meiosis-activating sterols in the formation of male and female germ cells.
source: t-MAS and its immediate precursor ff-MAS have been implicated as meiosis-activating sterols in the formation of male and female germ cells (Byskov et al., 1995)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

source: however, the role of these precursor sterols remains controversial.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

source: Germ-cell specific ablation of Cyp51a1, the enzyme that converts lanosterol to ff-MAS (Figure 1), markedly reduced testicular t-MAS concentration but had no effect on reproductive function in male mice (Keber et al., 2013).

claim: Approximately 5–10% of the lanosterol synthesized in the liver was converted to dihydrolanosterol, but not to downstream intermediates in the K–R pathway.
source: The liver was the only tissue in which we observed appreciable dihydrolanosterol synthesis (Figure 5). Approximately 5–10% of the lanosterol synthesized in the liver was converted to dihydrolanosterol, but not to downstream intermediates in the K–R pathway.
evidence: This is a finding from the in vivo flux analysis in liver.

claim: Labeled dihydrolanosterol did not appear in the plasma.
source: In contrast to other sterol intermediates synthesized in the liver, labeled dihydrolanosterol did not appear in the plasma (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a finding from the simultaneous measurement of sterol turnover in liver and plasma.

claim: The concentration of dihydrolanosterol in bile is not enriched relative to the liver.
source: Although we did not include biliary sterols in our flux studies, we have found that the concentration of dihydrolanosterol in bile is not enriched relative to the liver (data not shown).

claim: At least some of the dihydrolanosterol that is formed in the liver is converted to another sterol, the identity of which remains unknown.

claim: Dihydrolanosterol can promote degradation of HMG-CoA reductase.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that dihydrolanosterol can promote degradation of HMG-CoA reductase (Lange et al., 2008).

source: Therefore, one function of the dihydrolanosterol (or a metabolic derivative thereof) synthesized in the liver may be to provide rapid feedback inhibition of cholesterol biosynthesis through post-transcriptional regulation of HMG-CoA reductase.

source: Thus, cholesterol, or one or more of its biosynthetic precursors may be used for pheromone synthesis.

source: In contrast to skin and preputial gland, the brain has very low DHCR24 activity and was predicted to predominantly use the Bloch pathway (Nes, 2011).

source: Our data indicate other tissues with low rates of cholesterol synthesis, such as heart and skeletal muscle also predominantly used the MK–R pathway (Figure 5).

source: If the MK–R pathway is constitutive in vivo, as it appears to be in cultured cells, then predominant use of this pathway may ensure a constant rate of cholesterol synthesis in tissues that experience little variation in their cholesterol requirements.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the functional significance of pathway utilization.

claim: The relative utilization of the Bloch and MK–R pathways in cultured cells was strikingly similar to that observed in vivo in the tissue of origin.
source: The relative utilization of the Bloch and MK–R pathways in cultured cells was strikingly similar to that observed in vivo in the tissue of origin.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing pathway utilization in tissues versus cultured cells.

claim: The factors governing pathway selection are epigenetically fixed.
source: These findings suggest that the factors governing pathway selection are epigenetically fixed.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cultured cells retain the pathway preferences of their tissue of origin.

claim: Relative pathway utilization is presumably a function of the relative activities of the two enzymes at the branch point, which is tissue dependent.
source: Relative pathway utilization is presumably a function of the relative activities of the two enzymes at the branch point, which is tissue dependent.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the mechanism determining pathway utilization.

claim: Cell-type specific control of pathway utilization may involve epigenetic control of DHCR24 expression.
source: Since DHCR24 activity is a major determinant of relative pathway utilization, cell-type specific control of pathway utilization may involve epigenetic control of DHCR24 expression.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about the mechanism of pathway regulation.

claim: DHCR24 is phosphorylated at multiple sites and may be regulated at the post-translational level.
source: DHCR24 is phosphorylated at multiple sites and may be regulated at the post-translational level (Luu et al., 2014).

claim: The activity and substrate specificity of DHCR24 may be influenced by its intracellular location.
source: The activity and substrate specificity of the enzyme may also be influenced by its intracellular location.

claim: Brown and his colleagues reported that DHCR7 and DHCR24 co-immunoprecipitate in CHO-7 cells.
source: Brown and his colleagues reported that DHCR7 and DHCR24 co-immunoprecipitate in CHO-7 cells (Luu et al., 2015).

source: Those authors proposed that the formation of a complex between the two proteins favors the efficient conversion of 7-dehydrodesmosterol to desmosterol, and then to cholesterol.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior work, supported by citation.

source: This hypothesis is consistent with our finding that the Bloch pathway is predominantly used in steroidogenic cells.
evidence: This connects a prior hypothesis to the current findings.

claim: The patterns of deuterium enrichment of biosynthetic precursor sterols in plasma were similar to those seen in the liver, but distinct from those observed in extrahepatic tissues.
source: The patterns of deuterium enrichment of biosynthetic precursor sterols in plasma were similar to those seen in the liver, but distinct from those observed in extrahepatic tissues.

claim: The cholesterol pool in extrahepatic tissues is relatively isolated from the cholesterol in circulating lipoproteins.
source: This finding indicates that the cholesterol pool in extrahepatic tissues is relatively isolated from the cholesterol in circulating lipoproteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that plasma sterol labeling patterns match liver but not other tissues.

claim: Dietschy and colleagues reported that 80% of cholesterol biosynthesis in mice takes place in extra-hepatic tissues, while 80% of plasma low density lipoprotein cholesterol is taken up by the liver.
source: This hypothesis is supported by data from Dietschy and colleagues, who reported that 80% of cholesterol biosynthesis in mice takes place in extra-hepatic tissues, while 80% of plasma low density lipoprotein cholesterol is taken up by the liver (Osono et al., 1995).

claim: Most extrahepatic tissues obtain cholesterol primarily from de novo synthesis, with little contribution from circulating lipoproteins.
source: Thus, most extrahepatic tissues obtain cholesterol primarily from de novo synthesis, with little contribution from circulating lipoproteins.

claim: The effects of dietary and pharmacological interventions on cholesterol biosynthesis in the liver can be inferred from measurements of isotopic enrichment in the plasma.
source: This conclusion suggests that the effects of dietary and pharmacological interventions on cholesterol biosynthesis in the liver can be inferred from measurements of isotopic enrichment in the plasma.
evidence: This is a practical implication inferred from the finding that plasma sterol labeling mirrors liver.

claim: The approach used in this study could potentially be confounded by the presence of two pools of an intermediate in the pathway that turn over at different rates.
source: The approach used in this study could potentially be confounded by the presence of two pools of an intermediate in the pathway that turn over at different rates.
evidence: This is a discussion of potential limitations of the methodology.

source: The observation that multiple independent intermediates showed essentially identical kinetics argues against this possibility, but we cannot formally exclude it.
evidence: This is an argument based on the data that addresses a potential limitation.

claim: By combining LC-MS/MS methods with stable isotope tracing, flux can be monitored through multiple intermediates in a biosynthetic pathway simultaneously.
source: By combining LC-MS/MS methods with stable isotope tracing, flux can be monitored through multiple intermediates in a biosynthetic pathway simultaneously.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The approach of combining LC-MS/MS with stable isotope tracing can reveal bifurcations in established pathways that imply novel biochemistry and physiology for molecules previously viewed simply as biosynthetic intermediates.
source: As illustrated in the present study, this approach can reveal bifurcations in established pathways that imply novel biochemistry and physiology for molecules previously viewed simply as biosynthetic intermediates.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the broader implications of the methodological approach.
